# Watch the AI read a work order

Pick a document. On the left is the exact text the AI received. On the right is what it filled in, marked against the
[answer key](glossary.qmd#answer-key){.gl}. The [plain rules](glossary.qmd#rules){.gl} column shows what simple
search patterns found on the same page. Every document is [SYNTHETIC](glossary.qmd#synthetic){.gl}.

```{=html}
<div class="reader-controls" id="reader-controls" role="group" aria-label="Choose a document"></div>
<p class="reader-status" id="reader-status" aria-live="polite"></p>
```
:::

```{=html}
<div class="reader" id="reader">
  <noscript><p class="hl-panel">This page needs JavaScript to switch documents. Every wrong answer is also listed, with its document text, on <a href="errors.html">Where it slipped</a>.</p></noscript>
</div>
```

::: {.hl-panel .how-to}
## How to read this page

- **Highlights** show where each answer sits on the page. Each one carries the box number from the table.
- **✓ Right** means the AI's answer matches the answer key. **✗** says what went wrong: a wrong value, an invented
  value, or a blank.
- **Dotted underline: a decoy.** A last-service date or an hour-meter reading that looks like an answer but is not.
  They were planted on purpose.
- The highlight positions are found by this website's build script from the generator's label lists, not by the AI. The
  AI only returns the values.
- **Random document** picks any of the 50. **Show me a mistake** picks one of the documents the AI got at least one box
  wrong on, so the failures are easy to find.
:::
